title:	Cut over CI to RWX by removing the duplicate GitHub Actions workflows
state:	OPEN
author:	elviskahoro (elvis kahoro)
labels:	enhancement
comments:	1
assignees:	
projects:	
milestone:	
issue-type:	
parent:

sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	
blocking:	
number:	272
--
## Why
PR #269 added RWX ports of our CI (`.rwx/*.yml`) next to the GitHub Actions workflows and was merged on 2026-11-02 (merge commit 18f7f03). All four RWX checks were green on that PR. The GitHub Actions copies are now redundant, so every PR and merge-queue entry pays for CI twice. This issue is the cutover: delete the ported GHA workflows and make the Trunk merge queue gate on the RWX statuses instead.

The cutover is deliberately a second PR. RWX triggers only fire from the default branch, so required RWX statuses could not post on the PR that introduced them (same staging as sdk-python-attio #76).

## Scope
**Delete** (all ported to `.rwx/`):
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`
- `.github/workflows/trunk-check.yml`
- `.github/workflows/validate-assets.yml`
- `.github/workflows/trunk-impacted-targets.yml`

**Keep on GitHub Actions:** `.github/workflows/pullfrog.yml` (vendor-managed harness) and `.github/FUNDING.yml`. Both sibling repos (sdk-python-attio, sdk-python-linear) keep pullfrog on GHA too.

**Flip `merge.required_statuses` in `.trunk/trunk.yaml`** from the GHA job names to the RWX status names:

| Remove | Add |
| --- | --- |
| `Trunk Check` | `RWX: trunk-check` |
| `Tests` | `RWX: tests` |
| `Generate & Verify Docs and Social Cards` | `RWX: docs-and-assets` |

`RWX: trunk-impacted-targets` stays OUT of the list, same as the GHA `Upload Impacted Targets` job today: the queue waits on the upload itself, not on the check.

**Update the comments/docs that name the GHA workflows:**
- `.trunk/trunk.yaml` comment block above `merge.required_statuses` (says the first three are GitHub Actions check-runs, names the three workflow files, and says impacted targets are "authorized by the TRUNK_API_TOKEN repo secret").
- `AGENTS.md` lines ~40-58 (merge queue section; references `.github/workflows/trunk-impacted-targets.yml`).
- `.rwx/*.yml` header comments that say "Ports .github/workflows/..." can be reworded since those files will no longer exist.
- Grep for any other reference: `git grep -n "\.github/workflows" -- ':!.github'`.

## Order of operations (important, the queue can deadlock)
1. Open the PR deleting the four workflows and editing `.trunk/trunk.yaml`. Note that the PR's own checks will be the RWX ones only.
2. **Before merging**, confirm the RWX statuses post on a PR and on a `trunk-merge/**` queue branch: `gh pr checks <pr> --json name --jq '.[].name'` should list `RWX: trunk-check`, `RWX: tests`, `RWX: docs-and-assets`. Required status names must be live names or the queue never starts.
3. Because the old required checks (`Trunk Check`, `Tests`, `Generate & Verify ...`) will stop posting, check GitHub branch protection / the "main - PR requirements" ruleset for required checks by those old names and update them in the same window. `pullfrog-approval` is required on the GitHub side only and must stay.
4. Merge via the Trunk queue and watch the first queue entry go through green.

## Do not
- Do not add path filters or `workflow_run` triggers to any RWX file (a check that does not report on every PR deadlocks the queue). All four `.rwx` files currently have none.
- Do not add `RWX: trunk-impacted-targets` to `required_statuses`.
- Do not delete `pullfrog.yml`.
- Do not force-push or bypass hooks.

## Related cleanup (decide, don't assume)
- The `TRUNK_API_TOKEN` GitHub repo secret becomes unused once `trunk-impacted-targets.yml` is deleted. The RWX version reads `TRUNK_API_KEY` from the `buridan-ui-trunk` vault. Removing the repo secret is outward-facing; ask the repo owner first.
- `.github/dependabot.yml` does not exist. sdk-python-linear has one (github-actions ecosystem, weekly) to bump SHA pins in `pullfrog.yml`. Optional follow-up.
- Known low-severity review notes on the `.rwx` files, deferred from #269: `trunk-impacted-targets.yml` skips (exit 0) when `TRUNK_API_KEY` is empty instead of failing, and builds its JSON body by string interpolation; `validate-assets.yml` runs `uv sync --group dev` without `--frozen` (matches the old GHA workflow); on PRs `trunk-check` diffs against the merge-base rather than the merge ref, so a finding that landed on main in a file the PR also touches can fail until rebase.

## Verification
- `gh pr checks <pr-number>`: RWX statuses present and green; no old GHA check names pending.
- `trunk check` on the changed files (`.trunk/trunk.yaml`, `AGENTS.md`).
- A queued PR reaches merge through the Trunk queue with RWX statuses gating it.
- `git grep -n "Trunk Check\|Generate & Verify\|\.github/workflows"` shows no stale references.

## Reference
- Merged PR: #269
- Pattern: sdk-python-attio #76 (staged cutover); sdk-python-linear `.rwx/` and `.github/` (only `pullfrog.yml` + `dependabot.yml` remain there).
- RWX status naming: with `status-checks: name: X` the status is `RWX: X`.

Follow-up to the PR staging the RWX workflows (.rwx/*.yml).

Cutover: delete the GHA equivalents of tests, trunk-check, validate-assets and trunk-impacted-targets, and flip `merge.required_statuses` in .trunk/trunk.yaml. Only possible once the RWX workflows are on main and have run on real PRs.

Gaps roborev found in the port (deferred as design-level):
1. `.rwx/trunk-check.yml` lints the PR head against the merge-base, so a regression on a line main already fixed isn't reported. GHA diffs against main's tip. Fix: fetch `refs/pull/<n>/merge` and use `FETCH_HEAD^1`, or document the weaker base.
2. The RWX `pull_request` triggers have no `branches: [main]` restriction, unlike GHA.
3. `.rwx/trunk-impacted-targets.yml` has no author gate, so a fork PR may fail red on a locked-vault miss. Add an `if:` on pr-author as sdk-python-attio does, or verify empirically.

# git-hook-triggered actions disabled so trunk releases core.hooksPath to
    # Entire (checkpoints). trunk-check-pre-push is redundant with roborev + the
    # merge queue's required "Lint and type check with Trunk"; git-lfs is unused.
    - trunk-fmt-pre-commit
    - git-lfs

    - trunk-check-pre-push

merge:
  # These must be live GitHub status names posted on every PR targeting main.
  # Re-verify after any pipeline rename:
  #   gh pr checks <pr-number> --json name --jq '.[].name'
  # gh pr checks lists check-runs from any app, so it covers app-posted checks
  # such as pullfrog-approval too.
  #
  # The first three are RWX statuses ("RWX: <status-check name>") posted by
  # .rwx/trunk-check.yml, tests.yml, and validate-assets.yml. Each shares one
  # status-check name across pull_request and push events, so the queue sees
  # identical names on PRs and on its trunk-merge/** branches.
  #
  # pullfrog-approval (Pullfrog's AI review verdict, posted by the Pullfrog
  # GitHub App; distinct from the `pullfrog` agent-run check) is required on
  # the GitHub side only (ruleset "main - PR requirements" plus classic branch
  # protection on main, pinned to the Pullfrog app). That gates direct merges
  # and queue admission. It is deliberately NOT listed here, so the queue does
  # not wait for a fresh verdict on the state it tests.
  #
  # Do NOT add path-filtered workflows here (they do not report on every PR and
  # would deadlock the queue). Same for workflow_run-triggered workflows.
  #
  # Entire Gates stays excluded entirely (agent session tracking; not posted on
  # every PR).
  #
  # Graph mode also gates admission on impacted targets: the queue holds every
  # PR at Not Ready until targets have been uploaded for its head sha.
  # .rwx/trunk-impacted-targets.yml does that on every PR to main
  # (PUT /v2/impacted-targets, authorized by TRUNK_API_KEY from the
  # buridan-ui-trunk RWX vault). The status stays out of this list on purpose
  # -- the queue waits on the upload itself, not the check -- but a red
  # RWX: trunk-impacted-targets status means no
  # upload landed and queued PRs stall at Not Ready even with every required
  # status green.
  required_statuses:
    - "RWX: trunk-check"

---AGENTS.md---
on the final PR preview is the explicit human authorization to merge — after
it, submit with `trunk merge <pr-number>` without re-prompting. There is no
second gate before the merge lands.

The queue's required statuses live in `.trunk/trunk.yaml`
(`merge.required_statuses`) and must be live GitHub check names posted on
every PR. Re-verify after any pipeline rename:
`gh pr checks <pr-number> --json name --jq '.[].name'`. Do not add
path-filtered or `workflow_run`-triggered workflows there: they do not report
on every PR and would deadlock the queue.

Graph mode adds one more admission gate beyond `merge.required_statuses`: the
queue holds every PR at Not Ready until impacted targets have been uploaded
for its head sha. `.rwx/trunk-impacted-targets.yml` uploads them
on every PR to main (`PUT /v2/impacted-targets` authorized by
`TRUNK_API_KEY` from the `buridan-ui-trunk` RWX vault). The job stays out of
`merge.required_statuses` on purpose — the queue waits on the upload itself,
not the check — but a red `RWX: trunk-impacted-targets` status means nothing was
uploaded, and PRs stall at Not Ready even with every required status green.

`pullfrog-approval` (Pullfrog's AI review verdict) is required on the GitHub
side only (ruleset `main - PR requirements` plus classic branch protection on
`main`, pinned to the Pullfrog app). It is deliberately not in
`merge.required_statuses`, so the Trunk queue does not wait on it.

The search turned up RWX's documented way to conditionally fire a trigger, but no explicit example that filters pull requests by base branch.

- **Conditional triggers:** RWX's docs say triggers can use an `if` condition to decide whether to start a run. The docs illustrate this with a push trigger that only fires for the main branch, using an `if` expression on the git branch. I didn't find the same pattern shown for `pull_request`.

input.prompt: Show the full schema for the github pull_request trigger: what fields are available under the trigger (if, init, status-checks, actions, branches filters), what event fields are exposed (e.g. base branch / base ref), and whether an `if:` condition can be attached directly to a pull_request trigger (not just push). Quote the exact YAML example(s) given.

result.output:
The page doesn't include a full schema for the `pull_request` trigger. It documents a few options through examples and tables, so the list below covers only what it states.

**Trigger fields**

- **`actions`**: The only trigger option documented in detail. By default RWX fires on "[opened, reopened, synchronize]". Example:
  ```yaml
  on:
    github:
      pull_request:
        actions: [opened]
  ```
- **`init`**: Shown in an example that passes event values into tasks:
  ```yaml
  on:
    github:
      pull_request:
        init:
          commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
  ```
- **`if`**: Not shown on the `pull_request` trigger. The page says [Event Triggers](/docs/event-triggers) covers "generic options like `title`, `target`, and `if`," which suggests it's a generic option, but the page doesn't confirm it for `pull_request` or give an example.
- **`status-checks`**: Not mentioned.
- **`branches`**: Not mentioned. `target` is named only as a generic option linked to Event Triggers.

**Event fields**

- `event.git.branch`: the pull request branch
- `event.git.sha`: the head commit SHA of the pull request
- `event.git.ref`: the fully qualified ref, which "always starts with refs/heads/"
- `event.github.pull_request.number`: the pull request number
- `event.github.pull_request.pull_request.title`: the title (the path is written this way on the page)

There are no base branch or base ref fields listed. The page refers to GitHub's pull request webhook documentation for the full set of attributes under `event.github.pull_request`.

**Supported actions**

The page lists `closed`, `converted_to_draft`, `edited`, `labeled`, `opened`, `ready_for_review`, `reopened`, `synchronize`, and `unlabeled`. It says to contact RWX for other actions.

To confirm `if`, `status-checks`, `branches`, or base-ref fields, check the Event Triggers page and GitHub's webhook documentation.

input.prompt: Explain the generic trigger options "title", "target", and "if". Show exact YAML syntax for using "if" on a trigger (is it a sibling key to the trigger type like pull_request, or nested inside it? can it be a list of alternatives like push triggers with multiple `if` branches?). Quote exact examples.

result.output:
**Generic trigger options**

- **`title`** overrides the default run title. It accepts an expression and can use the `mint`, `event`, and `init` contexts. The docs give this example: `title: 'CI: ${{ event.github.push.head_commit.message}}'`.
- **`target`** limits a run to specific tasks. You can set it under any trigger, such as `push` or `pull_request`. For example, `target: task-key-to-run` runs one task. To run several, pass an array: `target: [task-key1, task-key2]`.
- **`if`** makes a trigger conditional, so a run starts only when the expression is true. The docs show it used with `push`.

**Syntax for `if`**

`if` is nested inside the trigger type, as a sibling of keys like `init` and `target`. It is not a sibling of `push` at the `on:` level. The documented example is:

```yaml
on:
  github:
    push:
      if: ${{ event.git.branch == 'main' }}
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
```

The structure is `on` → provider (`github`) → trigger type (`push`) → `if`, `init`, and so on. The same nesting applies to `pull_request`, since the docs say the generic options apply to all triggers, though the page shows no `pull_request` example with `if`.

**Can `if` be a list of alternatives?**

The page does not document this. It shows only a single `if` expression. The array form is documented for *multiple triggers*, where each item has its own `target` and `init`, and RWX creates one run per item. The page does not say whether each array item can have its own `if`, and it shows no multi-branch `if` syntax. If you need several conditions, test before relying on a particular form.

# Test gate for the Trunk merge queue (see .trunk/trunk.yaml: merge.required_statuses).
#
# - pull_request on main gates ordinary PRs.
# - push on trunk-merge/** is the Trunk merge queue testing a PR stack as if it
#   had already merged, so the queue catches tests that only fail on the merge
#   result, not just on the PR head.
# - push on main is the post-merge safety net, matching gtm-sdk's tests gate.
name: Tests

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - trunk-merge/**
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read
---trunk-check---
# Lint gate for the Trunk merge queue (see .trunk/trunk.yaml: merge.required_statuses).
#
# Trunk only fails on NEW issues (findings introduced relative to the upstream
# base), so the ~2k pre-existing findings on main do not block PRs; a PR passes
# by not making lint worse. `--ci` plus stdin redirection is required: without
# them trunk can hang on an interactive prompt in CI (observed in gtm-sdk).
#
# Trigger notes:
# - pull_request on main gates ordinary PRs against the merge ref's first
#   parent (HEAD^1): the exact, fresh main tip GitHub used to build
#   refs/pull/N/merge, the same base trunk-io/trunk-action's pull_request.sh
#   computes. github.event.pull_request.base.sha must NOT be used here -- it
#   is the base tip frozen at PR creation and never advances, so a long-lived
#   PR would lint all of main's drift since creation, and merging main into
#   the branch does not refresh it (only a rebase does).
# - push on trunk-merge/** is the Trunk merge queue testing a PR stack as if
#   it had already merged; HEAD^1 is the main tip the queue branch was stacked
#   on, so the diff is exactly the queued PRs' combined changes (the same base
#   trunk-action's trunk_merge.sh computes for queue branches).
# - There is deliberately no push-to-main lint run: on a push to main, HEAD
---validate-assets---
name: Docs & Assets

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - trunk-merge/**
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  validate-generated-assets:
    name: Generate & Verify Docs and Social Cards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
---impacted---
# Uploads impacted targets for the Trunk merge queue.
#
# The queue runs in graph (Parallel) mode, where Trunk holds every PR at "Not
# Ready" until impacted targets have been uploaded for its head commit. This repo
# is a single deployable unit, so every PR declares that it impacts everything
# (impactsAllTargets): the queue then serializes entries instead of testing them
# in parallel.
#
# Authenticates with the TRUNK_API_TOKEN repo secret (a Trunk API key). The
# trunk-io/login OIDC action returned HTTP 500 for this repo, so the REST
# endpoint is called directly:
# https://docs.trunk.io/merge-queue/reference/api-v2/impactedtargets/upload-a-pull-requests-impacted-targets
#
# Fork and Dependabot PRs get no secrets, so they skip the upload with a warning
# (green check) and stay at "Not Ready" until a maintainer re-pushes the branch
# from this repo.
#
# Do NOT add path filters here: a PR that skips this workflow never uploads, and
# the queue would hold it forever. Re-uploads on every push via `synchronize`.
name: Trunk Impacted Targets

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
